title: Indra evening cluster sprint notes
content:
Quick snapshot (evening sprint) - brain dump + what to hand off

Date: 2026-03-13 (end of day)
Owner: Indra Bhatt
Context: Lightweight personal scratchpad for node pool tidy, capacity checks, and a few networking flares that popped up during the afternoon load test. Not polished — for next-shift ops and follow-ups.

Topline items
- Pool B (us-east-1a) nearing sustained 78% GPU utilization during 90m spike; autoscaler reacted but we saw a tail of queued jobs (~3m avg queue time)
- Two intermittent pkt drops on tor-6 observed at 17:24 and 18:02 — likely transient, need follow-up with infra-networking during weekday
- One node (gpu-0452) OOM-killed a Cuda process at 16:48. Kernel message: out-of-memory -> restarted kworker, container restarted by kubelet. Suspect bad model run with mem leak.

Immediate TODOs (prioritize for morning)
1) Run quick capacity bake: snapshot per-pool usage and pad recommendations
   - query: SELECT pool, avg(util_gpu) as avg, p95(queue_ms), active_instances FROM capacity_metrics WHERE ts > now() - 2h AND pool IN ('pool-a','pool-b','pool-edge');
   - target: for pool-b, suggest +6 slots (g5x-large equiv) for next 24h if p95 queue > 2m
2) Flag gpu-0452 for soak and root-cause: cordon -> recreate -> run reproducer (model X, prompt batch 10k tokens)
   - commands: kubectl cordon gpu-0452; kubectl drain gpu-0452 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; open new node via infra-ops self-serve
3) Add tor-6 packet drop logs to a short incident note and ping netops in morning: @evan and @maya to loop in (see linked slack thread)
4) Move two long-running eval jobs (owner: @ml-evals) off of pool-b until we confirm the pad scaling prevents queueing
5) Small cleanup: reclaim 3 stale preemptible instances in pool-edge (ids: i-0a1b2c3d, i-0a1b2c3e, i-0a1b2c3f)

Notes / Observations (freeform)
- Autoscaler logs: saw 2 scale-up events at 16:30 and 17:10 but pods still queued for ~3m. Need to check launch time distribution — cold start for preemptibles is longer than we tolerate under burst windows. Consider prioritizing non-preemptible burst reserve for critical routes.
- Cache hit rate on prefix cache took a small dip during the test (cache-hit 0.69 -> 0.62). Might be caused by multiple evals with wide context lengths. Worth flagging in optimize notes.
- Reproducer for gpu-0452: when running reproduce.sh (linked in the PR), memory climbs gradually until oom. That reproducer only ran against CUDA 12.3 runtime. Confirm if node had mixed driver versions.

Commands I used / shorthand (copy pasta in morning)
- kubectl get nodes -l pool=pool-b -o wide
- kubectl describe node gpu-0452 | egrep -A3 'Non-terminated Pods\:|Allocatable|Capacity'
- journalctl -u kubelet --since '2026-03-13 16:00' | grep -i oom
- aws ec2 describe-instances --instance-ids i-0a1b2c3d i-0a1b2c3e i-0a1b2c3f --query 'Reservations[*].Instances[*].[InstanceId,State.Name,Tags]'
- ./infra-scripts/scale-pad.sh --pool pool-b --add 6 --reason 'evening spike 2026-03-13'

Handoff summary for next shift
- Expect follow-ups on: whether +6 pad for pool-b reduces p95 queue under 2m. If not, escalate to capacity squad for temporary reserved nodes.
- Netops: tor-6 drops — not a full outage but correlate with switch-level logs. Leave packet captures on for 24h.
- gpu-0452: we cordoned and recreated once; keep an eye on similar OOM traces across other nodes (pattern: long-running evals + spike in token length).
- Owners to ping: @maya (netops), @evan (capacity), @sophie (ml-evals job owners)

Open questions / things to think about
- Should we bias autoscaler to prefer non-preemptible nodes under sudden p95 queue surges? Cost tradeoff vs SLOs — ask finance for quick delta estimate.
- Is there a pattern where prefix cache dips during parallel eval bursts? If so, can we split evaluators by cache-key namespace to avoid colding out the prefix caches?
- How brittle are the model-run memory profiles across driver/runtime versions? Might need a small validation matrix in release engineering.

Mini checklist (safety and low-friction)
- [ ] Create INFRA-incident stub for tor-6 drops (attach logs)
- [ ] Post recap in #infra-gpu-ops with immediate actions taken
- [ ] Start reproduce job on fresh node when morning starts (mark in ticket)
- [ ] Add padding change to capacity sheet and note cost delta (rough estimate)

Random notes to self (brain dump)
- Look into longer warm-start for preemptible images (bake AMI with larger init ramdisk?)
- Follow PR 891 — kernel selection tweak might reduce OOM likelihood when mixed quant tables are used
- Ask product if any customer experiments are scheduled on pool-b for next 48h (don't want to overlap)

Useful links / refs
- Reproducer script: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/tools/reproduce/gpu-oom.sh
- Capacity dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/capacity/pool-overview
- Autoscaler logs: s3://redwood-ops-logs/autoscaler/2026/03/13/

End of notes.
